In summary, our research is concerned with
the simulation and characterization of gate dielectric reliability issues.
the statistical modeling and simulation of gate dielectrics.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the simulation of gate leakage and dielectric breakdown is possible with a high degree of accuracy.
the models presented in this work provide a good basis for a reliable simulation of gate leakage and breakdown effects.
the gate leakage and wear out models are useful tools to understand and predict the impact of gate leakage and dielectric wearout on CMOS circuit performance and reliability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the models are able to describe the gate dielectric degradation process in a very realistic way and that the models are useful for the simulation of the degradation process of standard CMOS circuits.
gate dielectric wear out can not only be simulated but that the models can also be used to characterize the gate dielectric material and the gate oxide process.
gate leakage is a major issue in advanced CMOS devices and that the leakage-induced degradation of the device characteristics can be reduced by the use of high-k dielectrics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the leakage-induced wearout is the most important degradation mechanism for ZrO ₂ -based gate stacks.

gate dielectric degradation is a very complex phenomenon that is strongly affected by the device structure, and that it is necessary to take into account the spatial distribution of defects and traps in the dielectric in order to obtain a realistic picture of gate degradation.
, for the simulation of the leakage, wearout and breakdown of gate dielectric layers, it is crucial to include the effects of the leakage on the dielectric layer.
